title: Regional anchoring and staggered evacuation policy for Dedicated fleets
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Problem: Customers using Dedicated capacity with regulatory or contractual data residency requirements need predictable throughput and graceful behavior when zones or regions lose capacity. Current placement places pods by least-loaded scheduling which causes churn during autoscale bursts and can violate residency constraints or create sudden throughput loss during failover.

Goal: Implement a regional anchoring + staggered evacuation policy that: (1) allows fleets to declare residency constraints (hard/soft anchors) and preferred zone weightings, (2) exposes throughput guarantees tied to dedicated pool size and placement policy, (3) coordinates with autoscaling so we avoid mass simultaneous drains, and (4) provides clear operational playbooks and observability for failover events. The feature should be compatible with existing Dedicated routing and fallback layers and enable per-customer residency enforcement without sacrificing average throughput for non-residency customers.
acceptance_criteria: Customers can mark a dedicated pool as 'region-anchored' with a preference ranking of zones (API + Console).

Scheduler honors hard residency constraints and only places resources in allowed regions; soft anchors prefer zones but allow temporary cross-zone placement during emergencies with annotated reason codes.

Autoscaler integrates with staggered evacuation policy: when scaling down or draining a zone, instances are drained in waves (configurable window) to preserve throughput SLOs and reduce cold-start pressure in remaining zones.
Routing layer respects residency flags for incoming requests and will not route requests subject to hard residency to non-compliant endpoints; audit logs capture routing decisions.
Playbook + dashboards exist to detect and respond to cross-zone capacity loss within target MTTR; SLOs for failover latency are instrumented.
E2E tests cover normal scale, surge traffic, single-zone outage, and full-region failover scenarios with assertions for throughput and data residency compliance.
implementation_notes: Scheduler changes: add zone_preference vector (float weights) and residency_mode enum (hard | soft | none) to pool config; use scoring function that multiplies base score by zone_preference and enforces hard residency by filtering nodes.
Anchoring behavior: soft anchors allow up to X% of capacity to be placed outside preferred zones during emergency (configurable per-customer), record eviction_reason metadata for auditability.

Staggered evacuation: implement drain-waves with jittered start times per-availability-zone and per-pool cooldown to avoid simultaneous cold starts; integrate with admission controller to limit new placements into draining zones.

Autoscaler hooks: when decision to scale_down triggers, autoscaler emits zone-drain-intent events to orchestrator which then executes wave-based eviction, with backoff if downstream latency or throughput degrades beyond thresholds.
Routing: enrich route planner policy with residency tags; fallback chains include same-region compatible models and a deny-when-hard-residency-violated option for enforcement.
Data and audit: persist placement decisions, eviction reasons, and residency tags in event store and surface in Console and logs for compliance review.
Backward compatibility: default residency_mode to none for existing pools; migration path provided for customers to opt into anchoring with validation checks.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): enable anchoring flags in test clusters and run synthetic workloads for two weeks (internal only).
Phase 1 (beta): offer region-anchoring as opt-in for select enterprise customers with dedicated pools; monitor throughput and residency compliance; collect feedback.
Phase 2 (general): enable in Console and API for all Dedicated customers, defaulting to soft anchors with conservative emergency thresholds.
Phase 3 (enforcement): allow admins to enable hard-residency enforcement with security review and contractual ticketing.
test_plan: Unit tests for scheduler scoring and filtering rules for residency_mode and zone_preference vectors.
Integration tests for autoscaler orchestrator interaction, verifying drain waves and backoff behavior under synthetic load spikes.
Chaos test: simulate single AZ and full-region failures; assert failover TTL for throughput and confirm audit logs for cross-zone placements.
Compliance test: verify routing denies requests subject to hard residency when only non-compliant endpoints exist.
Load test: ensure throughput guarantees (as documented in SLA) are met within 95th percentile under normal and surge conditions for anchored pools.
monitoring_slo_metrics: regional.failover.latency.p95: time from AZ down signal to 80% traffic re-routed to compliant endpoints
pool.throughput.per_node: tokens/sec per instance during normal and drain phases
placement.compliance.rate: percentage of placements matching hard residency constraints
drain.wave.success: percent of waves completed without triggering autoscaler emergency throttles
audit.log.ingest.latency: time to persist placement/audit events
decisions: Use soft anchors by default to reduce customer surprise; hard anchors require explicit opt-in and a security review.
Staggered evacuation implemented in orchestrator layer rather than kernel-level to simplify rollout and minimize runtime coupling.
Allow per-pool emergency cross-zone threshold (default 10%) to balance availability vs strict residency.
Expose residency flags in both API and Console for transparency and operational control.
open_questions: How should billing behave if soft-anchored traffic spills into other regions? Charge by actual execution region or by pool region?
What is the maximum acceptable emergency cross-zone percentage before legal/compliance escalation is required?
Do we require per-customer KMS isolation for hard-residency pools or is network-level zoning sufficient for initial launch?
Should the drain waves be coordinated globally per-region or independently per-pool to reduce blast radius?
